title: streaming: robust lifecycle controls for client cancel, disconnect, and reconnect/resume
author: Maria Chen
description: Motivation: production services saw intermittent outages and user-facing truncated streams when clients disconnect abruptly or attempt to resume after network blips. This PR adds explicit lifecycle controls for streaming responses to (1) let clients cancel in-band, (2) gracefully handle TCP disconnects on the server, and (3) allow authenticated reconnect/resume with server-side timeouts and resource reclamation. What this changes: implement a lifecycle manager in the streaming runtime to track streams, expose an id+resume_token to clients for reconnect attempts, propagate client-cancel signals across runtime and model backends, and ensure server-side inactivity/timeouts reclaim KV cache and batch slots. Also update the OpenAI-compat adapter so resume and cancel semantics match common client expectations (stream end vs error events). Behavioral details and guarantees: - Client cancel: clients may send an explicit cancel frame (X-Client-Cancel) or rely on HTTP/2 stream reset; the runtime will mark stream canceled and attempt immediate model-level cancellation, returning a final "cancel" event to the client when cancel completes. - Disconnects: on TCP/connection loss the server keeps a short grace window (configurable, default 30s) allowing clients to reconnect with the resume token. During the grace window work is soft-cancelled but KV cache retained. - Reconnect/Resume: clients can reconnect using the stream_id + resume_token header. The runtime verifies token, rebinds KV cache, and attempts to resume decoding from last confirmed token (best-effort; may re-run up to last checkpoint). - Server timeouts: long-idle/incomplete streams are reclaimed after two configurable timers: grace_window (default 30s) and reclamation_window (default 300s). After reclamation the resume token is invalidated and resources freed. Compatibility notes: - OpenAI-compat adapter now emits the same sequence of events as OpenAI in cancel/disconnect cases (data/error/close ordering) and maps Redwood resume behavior to a custom "resume_token" header; documentation and SDKs are updated. - SDKs: minor Python SDK changes to expose resume headers and convenience helpers (see CHANGELOG entries). Tests and rollout: unit tests for lifecycle manager, integration tests with simulated disconnects, e2e in perf-canary cluster. Feature gated behind runtime flag 'streaming_lifecycle_v2' and rolled out via canary -> staged -> global over 2 weeks. Checklist: - [x] implement lifecycle manager and server timeouts - [x] add OpenAI-compat adapter updates - [x] add unit/integration tests - [x] add docs + SDK CHANGELOG - [x] feature flag + canary rollout plan Related: Linked Linear tickets ENG-1243 (streaming lifecycle design), ENG-1301 (openai compat resume semantics).

release_notes: Improves streaming robustness: client-initiated cancel, graceful disconnect handling with resume token support, and server-side inactivity reclaiming. Backward-compatible by default; feature gated behind streaming_lifecycle_v2. SDKs updated to expose resume helpers.

Operations rollout notes: start 5% canary -> 25% -> 100% if no errors and resumed stream success rate > 99% over 24h.
